=== Header ===
Designed via CSDP on 2026-10-15, 1 dialogue turn (rules.md), mode=one-shot.
Model urn:gnd:registrar@1, version 4. The spring catalogue is a fixed reference
population (references/catalog.pop.json, sha256 d8e36bad…5792).

Legend: lines with no prefix are the registrar's own rules (explicit, confirmed,
hard). [PROPOSED …] lines were inferred and are advisory until you confirm them.

=== Object Types ===
Student is identified by StudentName. A Student may exist without playing any
role (a newly admitted student has no enrollments yet).
Course is identified by CourseCode.
Term is identified by TermName.
StudentName, CourseCode, TermName, CourseTitle and Grade are values of type String.
CreditCount and CreditLoad are values of type Integer.

=== Fact Types ===
Course has CourseTitle.                            [fixed catalogue]
  [PROPOSED, from the catalogue sample] Each Course has at most one CourseTitle.
  [PROPOSED, from the catalogue sample] Each Course has some CourseTitle.
  Sample: CS101 has 'Intro to Programming'; CS340 has 'Machine Learning'.

Course is worth CreditCount.                       [fixed catalogue]
  [PROPOSED, from the catalogue sample] Each Course is worth at most one CreditCount.
  [PROPOSED, from the catalogue sample] Each Course is worth some CreditCount.
  Sample: CS101 is worth 4; STAT210 is worth 3.

Course needs Course (prerequisite).                [fixed catalogue]
  Each Course needs a given prerequisite Course at most once.
  [PROPOSED, LLM-inferred] No Course needs itself, directly or through a chain
    (prerequisites are acyclic). Why: a cycle would make every course on it
    impossible to take.
  Sample: CS340 needs CS230; CS340 needs MATH220; CS230 needs CS101.

Course requires Course (prerequisite).             [derived]
  Derived: Course C requires Course P if C needs P, or C needs some Course M
  that requires P. (This is the "directly or through a chain" rule.)

Course is offered in Term.                         [fixed catalogue]
  Each Course is offered in a given Term at most once.
  Sample: CS101 is offered in spring; CS250 is offered in fall.

Student is enrolled in Course for Term.
  Each Student is enrolled in a given Course for a given Term at most once.
  Each Student is enrolled in at most 6 Courses for each Term.

Student has passed Course.
  Each Student has passed a given Course at most once.
  Sample: Maya has passed CS101; Maya has passed MATH120; Maya has passed CS230.

Student received Grade for Course.
  Each Student received at most one Grade for each Course.

Student carries CreditLoad in Term.                [derived]
  Derived: a Student's CreditLoad in a Term is the sum of the credits of the
  Courses that Student is enrolled in for that Term.

=== Top-level Constraints ===
If a Student is enrolled in Course C for a Term, and C requires Course P,
  then that Student has passed P.
If a Student is enrolled in Course C for a Term, then that Student has not
  passed C.
If a Student carries CreditLoad N in a Term, then N is at most 18.
If a Student is enrolled in Course C for Term T, then C is offered in T.
[PROPOSED, LLM-inferred] If a Student received a Grade for Course C, then that
  Student has passed C. Why: "Record a grade, which also marks the course as
  passed" — this assumes there are no failing grades.

=== Operations ===
Enroll Student in Course for Term.
  Requires: Course is offered in Term.
  Effect: asserts Student is enrolled in Course for Term.
  Frame: an undeclared side effect is a warning (deontic).

Drop Course for Student in Term.
  Effect: retracts Student is enrolled in Course for Term.
  Frame: deontic.

Drop every course Student takes in Term.
  Effect: retracts every enrollment of Student for Term.
  Frame: deontic.

Record Grade for Student in Course (for Term).
  Effects: asserts Student received Grade for Course; asserts Student has passed
  Course; retracts Student is enrolled in Course for Term.
  Rule: once recorded, a Student's Grade for a Course never changes.
  Frame: deontic.

Admit Student.
  Effect: creates a new Student.
  Frame: deontic.

=== Open questions (not decided by rules.md) ===
1. Is the frame on every operation a warning (current draft) or a hard failure?
2. Record Grade retracting the enrollment is a modeling choice; it reads
   "enrolled" as "currently registered". Is that right?
3. Can a grade be a fail? The rules say every recorded grade marks the course
   passed.
4. Are students identified by name, or do they have a student number?
5. Terms are just "spring" and "fall" with no year. Should a term carry a year?

I built the registrar model from `rules.md`. `gnd validate` passes on the full model (exit 0, no warnings), so both structural and semantic layers were checked.

**Files** (in the working directory):
